A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SG-ULA research work. The main text, equations, Tables 1–2, and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched reliably across the revision.

before.justification: v1 contains mathematical examples, convergence proofs, and analytic complexity tables, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. The added SCAD example supplies mathematical derivations, not empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 5 retain the same SG-ULA subgradient update, Gaussian noise, and subgradient-selection convention. The SCAD addition illustrates another potential without changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for training or empirical evaluation. Section 4.3's SCAD example introduces no evaluated data or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Lehec, Johnston et al., Habring et al., and Fruehwirth et al., with the same theoretical comparisons against SG-ULA. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental protocols or configurations. Changes to temperature restrictions and step-size guarantees concern theorem conditions, assessed under T1.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablation, sensitivity, robustness, or empirical case-study results. The new SCAD section verifies mathematical properties of an example and is assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated trials, seeds, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Expectations appearing in the proofs are theoretical quantities.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains identical complexity orders in every method–metric entry. Neither PDF contains empirical result entries; revisions to symbolic bounds and constants are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 adds SCAD definitions and convexification arguments in Section 4.3. It revises Theorem 3/Lemma 11's excess-risk bound and M, restricts Theorem 3 to beta >= 4/mu, corrects Corollary 3's squared constant to a fourth power, and derives an explicit stationary-moment bound in Lemma 10. Appendix C/Table 2 also change C_r1 from 2C'_0/beta to 2/(beta C'_0) and replace L with K in the W2 contraction constants. These substantively revise formal guarantees despite retaining the headline convergence orders.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same central claims: sampling without smoothing under non-smooth, non-logconcave potentials, Wasserstein convergence guarantees, and associated excess-risk bounds. No new headline contribution or novelty claim appears.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds an applicability discussion connecting the framework to SCAD regularization, sparse estimation, and compressed sensing. Section 4.1 also explicitly qualifies the higher-dimensional extension by requiring convexity at infinity. Existing interpretations of dimension and nonconvexity dependence remain.

D1.justification: No code or data access instructions, implemented hyperparameter configurations, hardware, runtime, or data-processing details are added or revised. The added analytic constants and SCAD derivations concern theoretical documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Fan and Li (2001) and connects the framework to nonconcave penalized estimation through SCAD. The existing sampling literature and comparative positioning remain essentially unchanged; other bibliography revisions mainly update metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes local grammar, terminology, notation, and affiliation edits, clarifies the introductory excess-risk formulation, and adds subsection 4.3. The main section sequence and Appendix A–F organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 uses smaller body type, narrower margins, and more compact equation layouts. Both tables are reformatted, and Table 2 expands from 20 to 21 rows with a separate M entry. No figures or additional comparison tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 usefully corrects Corollary 3 and aligns Theorem 3's temperature restriction with Lemma 11, while adding an explicit moment bound and SCAD example. However, the new SCAD semi-convexity parameter conflicts by a factor of two with Definition 1's convention, and Proposition 4 reciprocates an unchanged C'_0 without a revised derivation. These mathematical reliability concerns coexist with identifiable corrections and explanatory gains, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
